knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Air-drying avoids re-contamination from a cloth or hands. The other options introduce a new contamination route or a non-sanitised rinse.
Hot-water sanitising depends on reaching a set temperature for a set time, so the temperature is checked rather than estimated.
A sanitised item can pick up microorganisms from an unclean surface, so storage must be clean and separate.

practicalCriteria: Observer confirms the learner checks temperature or concentration and starts the contact timer (pass: both recorded).
Observer confirms that all surfaces are covered for the full contact time (pass: no part missed).
Learner air-dries the item on a clean rack and stores it apart from raw materials (pass: no towel used; storage recorded).
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Observer checklist for the sanitising sequence
Batch record with temperature or concentration and contact time
Photo of the storage rack, taken with consent
stopWorkCriteria: The item still carries visible soil.
The water temperature or concentration cannot be confirmed.
The contact time cannot be maintained because the surface will dry or the solution is spent.
A sprayer or tank is leaking near the worker.
